title: Bridging Front-Door Adjustment and Information Bottleneck for Identifiable Causal Representations

problem.claim: Information Bottleneck can learn intermediate representations contaminated by spurious correlations and lacking causal validity under unobserved confounding.

gap.claim: Front-door adjustment provides criteria for identifying causal mediators but traditionally relies on known or preset mediator variables and is difficult to learn directly from data.

contributions.claim: FDA-IB embeds front-door causal identification conditions into the Information Bottleneck optimization process.
The framework converts front-door mediator generation and confounding blocking into HSIC-based optimization objectives.
The approach enables end-to-end learning of causal mediators from random sample pairs.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on multiple standard benchmarks reportedly show significantly improved out-of-distribution generalization performance.
The authors report that code is available in a GitHub repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: Information Bottleneck learns compressed intermediate variables for prediction.
Unobserved confounding can make IB mediators spuriously correlated and causally invalid.
Front-door adjustment offers identification criteria but is difficult to learn when mediators are not preset.
FDA-IB incorporates front-door conditions and HSIC objectives into IB to learn causal-relevant representations.
Benchmark experiments reportedly improve out-of-distribution generalization.

source_observation.claim: Causal identification conditions can be expressed as optimizable HSIC objectives within representation learning.

interpretation.claim: A theoretical causal criterion may become operational when translated into trainable independence or blocking objectives.

application.claim: When designing representations under confounding, consider incorporating domain-specific causal constraints directly into the learning objective.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the approach works beyond the reported benchmark settings or under different confounding structures.

unknowns: The specific benchmarks, baselines, metrics, and numerical effect sizes are not provided.
The abstract does not specify the assumptions, data requirements, or optimization details needed for causal identification.
The abstract does not independently verify the reported performance or code availability.
